question: How many images went into the DDQA-set, and from how many existing anomaly datasets were they taken?
answer_hint: 127,997 images drawn from four existing industrial anomaly detection datasets.

question: What four kinds of question does the DDQA-set cover?
answer_hint: Anomaly discrimination, rough defect localization, defect fine mapping (bounding boxes), and defect classification.

question: In EIAD, how is the language model's output turned into a pixel mask of the defect?
answer_hint: A special [SEG] token's last-layer embedding is projected and used to prompt the SAM decoder.

question: What LoRA ranks, learning rate and batch size did the EIAD authors use when fine-tuning their two modules?
answer_hint: EDDM: LoRA rank 8, alpha 32. MDLM: rank 16, alpha 16, 200 steps, lr 2e-3, batch 8.

question: What happened to EIAD's segmentation scores when the description module (EDDM) was removed?
answer_hint: Small drop: AUROC 87.8 to 87.0 on MVTec AD, 91.9 to 90.7 on VisA.

question: What weakness of existing multimodal defect detectors that are fine-tuned with grounding supervision does EIAD try to address?
answer_hint: They overfit during grounding-supervised fine-tuning, hurting generalization and the balance between QA and grounding.

question: How many images and how many questions are in the test data Reason-IAD is evaluated on?
answer_hint: 8,366 sampled images and 39,672 generated questions.

question: Which four image datasets make up the MMAD benchmark used to evaluate Reason-IAD?
answer_hint: MVTec-AD, VisA, MVTec-LOCO and GoodsAD.

question: What reward signal guides the optimisation of Reason-IAD's latent think tokens?
answer_hint: One minus the mean prediction entropy over latent tokens, optimised with a REINFORCE-style policy gradient.

question: How are Reason-IAD's latent tokens perturbed to explore the latent space?
answer_hint: Gaussian noise is added to the tokens at every iteration, at a 10% perturbation scale.

question: In the zero-shot MMAD setting, what average accuracy does Reason-IAD reach with Qwen3-VL-8B?
answer_hint: 76.71% average accuracy, versus 72.18% for the plain Qwen3-VL-8B.

question: How much does the retrieval-augmented knowledge module improve Qwen2.5-VL-7B on defect classification?
answer_hint: Defect classification accuracy rises from 55.23% to 67.97%.

question: What limitations of Reason-IAD do its authors acknowledge?
answer_hint: Slower than single-pass MLLMs due to multi-step latent reasoning; depends on the base MLLM following instructions.

question: What kinds of images did Reason-IAD get wrong in its reported failure cases?
answer_hint: A large defect spanning regions was mislocalized; a missing pushpin in a cluttered scene was called normal.

question: On which four benchmarks is the ReAL/CGRO method evaluated?
answer_hint: MVTec-AD, WFDD, SDD and DTD, under a zero-shot setting.
review_note: Trimmed broad gold: p7 dropped; p6, p8 and p15 all name the four benchmarks.

question: How does ReAL decide which reasoning tokens contribute to the anomaly map?
answer_hint: Keeps tokens with high semantic relevance to anomaly words and low spatial attention entropy; weights and sums their attention.

question: What averaged pixel-level AUROC does the full ReAL+CGRO model reach, compared with the vanilla Qwen2.5-VL-7B?
answer_hint: About 80.7 for the full model versus 64.7 for the vanilla model.

question: Which defect classes were held out as unseen when testing VLM-AOI?
answer_hint: Missing_hole and Spurious_copper.
review_note: Trimmed broad gold: p6 dropped; p3-p5 all name both unseen classes.

question: In VLM-AOI's first stage, how are candidate defect regions found?
answer_hint: PatchCore compares patches to a memory bank of normal features; thresholded map's connected components become boxes.

question: How were the regions of interest supplied to the classification stage during VLM-AOI's evaluation?
answer_hint: Ground-truth DeepPCB boxes were fed directly, so detection errors did not affect classification results.

question: On the seen defect classes, how did VLM-AOI compare with the few-shot ResNet-50 baseline?
answer_hint: VLM-AOI was worse: 61.3% versus 78.3% overall accuracy.

question: Which PCB defect types does VLM-AOI tend to confuse, and what do the authors blame?
answer_hint: Spur with Mouse_bite or Spurious_copper, and Short with Open_circuit; attributed to semantic ambiguity.

question: Which vision-language models were tried as the first-stage describer in Language Meets Vision?
answer_hint: Six: GPT4-Vision, Llama-3.2-11B-vision, Gemini Flash 1.5 (8B), Qwen2-VL-7B, LLaVA-v1.5-7B, Phi-3.5-vision.

question: How many parameters and FLOPs does the Language Meets Vision segmentation model have?
answer_hint: About 32.5M parameters and 58.7 GFLOPs.
edits: question made self-contained by naming the paper or method

question: What per-image inference time does Language Meets Vision report for its model, with and without quantization?
answer_hint: 52 ms per image, falling to 37 ms with quantization.
edits: question made self-contained by naming the paper or method

question: In Language Meets Vision, how does the hybrid decoding scheme set beam width and sampling temperature?
answer_hint: Narrow beams for detection/localization, wider for explanation; low temperature when uncertainty is under a threshold.
edits: question made self-contained by naming the paper or method

question: What loss function trains the segmentation network in Language Meets Vision?
answer_hint: Pixel-level cross-entropy plus a weighted Dice loss.

question: In the Language Meets Vision ablation, how much does the full multimodal fusion improve Dice over the ViT-only baseline?
answer_hint: From 88.0% to 93.9% Dice.
edits: question made self-contained by naming the paper or method

question: What open challenges do the Language Meets Vision authors acknowledge?
answer_hint: Anomalies on small objects and fine details remain hard to localize; foundation models need continued refinement.

question: How sensitive is the Language Meets Vision framework to which VLM writes the stage-1 descriptions?
answer_hint: Noticeably: GPT4-Vision text rated 5/5, Gemini 4/5, Llama-3.2 lower; text quality affects segmentation.
edits: question made self-contained by naming the paper or method

question: Which papers report their own method's average accuracy on the MMAD benchmark, and what is it?
answer_hint: EIAD about 69.4% (zero-shot); Reason-IAD on Qwen3-VL-8B about 79.4% one-shot, 76.71% zero-shot.

question: How is CLIP used across these papers?
answer_hint: VLM-AOI classifies cropped regions with CLIP; Reason-IAD retrieves category knowledge with it; Language Meets Vision uses it as a baseline.
review_note: Gold kept: BM25 top page 2602 p3 is related work about other methods' CLIP use.

question: Which source datasets appear both in EIAD's DDQA-set and in the CGRO training set?
answer_hint: Vision, PD-REAL/PR-REAL, Real-IAD and BSData appear in both.

question: Do Reason-IAD and the ReAL paper have the model write out its reasoning as text?
answer_hint: Reason-IAD reasons in latent tokens instead of explicit chains; ReAL generates textual reasoning and reads its attention.
review_note: ReAL gold trimmed to p2-p4: abstract p1 dropped, method page p4 kept.

question: How much energy per inspected image do these anomaly detectors consume on an embedded device such as a Jetson board?
answer_hint: Not reported in any paper.

question: How well do these methods detect weld defects in X-ray or CT inspection images?
answer_hint: Not addressed; no paper evaluates radiographic or CT data.

question: How many annotator hours did it take to build the DDQA dataset?
answer_hint: Not reported; EIAD only says rule-based construction is cheaper.

question: Which papers in my library use vision-language models?
answer_hint: All five: EIAD, Reason-IAD and ReAL/CGRO build on MLLMs; VLM-AOI uses CLIP; Language Meets Vision uses VLM descriptions.
edits: added: library-level question, gold at paper level with one evidence page per paper
